parts.meaning: The volume in the recipe, measured spooned and levelled.
The grams in one cup of whole wheat flour, from King Arthur Baking's chart.
The weight on the scale. It does not change with how you fill the cup.

howToSteps.name: Fluff the flour
howToSteps.text: Stir the flour in its bag or canister with a spoon a few times. Whole wheat flour settles in storage like any flour, and fluffing it up is what makes the cup weigh 113 grams.

howToSteps.name: Spoon it into the cup
howToSteps.text: Spoon the flour into the measuring cup until it heaps over the top. Do not scoop with the cup itself. Scooping packs the bran down and the cup weighs more.

howToSteps.name: Level it off
howToSteps.text: Sweep the flat edge of a knife across the rim of the cup, back into the bag. The cup is now level and holds one cup.

howToSteps.name: Convert or weigh
howToSteps.text: Weigh the flour if you have a scale: one level cup should read 113 grams. Or use the converter above. Cups times 113 is grams, grams divided by 113 is cups.

name: Whole Wheat Flour
sourceNote: King Arthur Baking lists whole wheat flour at 113 g per cup (4 oz).
title: Whole Wheat Flour Cups to Grams
tutorial: Whole wheat flour is lighter than white flour by the cup. One cup, spooned and levelled, weighs 113 grams, against 120 grams for all-purpose flour. The reason is what is still in it. Whole wheat flour keeps the bran and the germ, and those coarse flakes do not pack down the way fine white flour does. More air stays between the particles, so the cup holds less weight.

Measure it the same way as any flour. Fluff it with a spoon, spoon it into the cup until it heaps, then sweep a knife across the rim. Do not scoop with the cup. A scooped cup packs the flour down and the weight climbs, which throws off the recipe.

The converter works in both directions. Cups become grams when you want the scale to settle it. Grams become cups when the recipe is in grams and you are measuring by volume. Both directions use the same number: 113 grams per cup.

The anchor to remember is the pair. One cup is 113 grams, two cups is 226 grams. Half a cup is about 57 grams. Two cups of whole wheat flour weigh the same as one cup of butter, which is a strange fact and exactly why it sticks in my head.

One thing worth knowing: whole wheat flour drinks more water than white flour. The bran soaks it up. A recipe written for white flour needs a little extra liquid when you swap in whole wheat, and the dough benefits from a rest so the bran can hydrate. It also goes stale faster. The oils in the bran turn rancid at room temperature, so the bag keeps best in the fridge or the freezer.
